opening: Rain had found its way into the North Annex before anyone noticed the warped crate in the intake bay. Inside lay a water-damaged astronomical astrolabe, its rings dulled and its calibration tokens sealed in a trembling film of grit. The object had passed through the workshop’s imaging room, solvent bench, drying vault, and documentation office, leaving behind records that overlapped without agreeing. Five participants remained plausible. Rather than trust seniority, memory, or the apparent order of the rooms, the reviewers rebuilt the case from the surviving notes and the workshop’s own arithmetic.

scenes.prose: Before anyone compared the five names, the panel unfolded the board’s governing notice. For this incident, it declared the certified restoration lead protocol active; ordinary rank and reputation did not count. The reviewers then fixed one status scale for the entire inquiry: dormant was 0, waking 1, clear 2, stable 3, latent 4, and open 5. They wrote the local tally procedure beside it so that no later judgment could depend on an unstated convention. The tally began at 12. In the order relation, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol, each step squared the current tally, added the relevant coefficient times that stream’s status value, and retained the remainder modulo 97. The coefficients, in that order, were 13, 2, 3, 7, 5, and 11. The panel made three passes: first in the stated order, then in reverse order with the coefficients reversed, and then once more in the stated order with the coefficient list rotated one place to the left. It did not reset the tally between passes. Instead, it repeated that complete three-pass cycle 121 times.
scenes.title: The Governing Notes

scenes.prose: The first bundle came from the intake pairing sheet and the damaged roster. A torn corner still showed Val Sato’s apprentice lineage as open, while the surviving line for Winter Cohen remained latent. The reviewers set those pages beneath the lamp and moved on to the records that could anchor movement and consequence. A clock-backed entry placed Finley Meier’s work interval at latent. At the solvent bench, the chemical response following Parker Meier registered as stable; a separate causal review marked Oakley Brooks’s chemical response latent. The room question required a different kind of check: door and route marks placed Val Sato’s workshop room at waking, while corridor witnesses put Winter Cohen’s workshop room at clear. In the treatment sequence, reconstruction kept Finley Meier’s order at waking. Finally, a close photograph of the token set fixed Parker Meier’s tool stamp at waking, whereas the final count left Oakley Brooks’s stamp dormant.
scenes.title: Pairings, Doors, and Tokens

scenes.prose: A second packet had been sealed after a witness checked the roster. That witness left Parker Meier’s apprentice lineage clear, and the clerks’ worksheet, despite its water-blurred margin, wrote dormant beside Oakley Brooks’s. Timing evidence was more legible: clocked entries put Val Sato’s work interval at stable, while the sequence sheet showed Winter Cohen’s at waking. The chemical trail led elsewhere. Downstream checks tied Finley Meier to an open chemical response, a reading the reviewers compared against the movement sketch that marked Parker Meier’s workshop room as open. Oakley Brooks’s route ledger placed that workshop room at latent. At the documentation table, the ordered log gave Val Sato’s treatment order as open and Winter Cohen’s as dormant. Inventory then supplied the final check for this packet, counting Finley Meier’s tool stamp as stable.
scenes.title: The Sealed Worksheet

scenes.prose: The last reconstruction packet began with an earlier pairing note: Finley Meier’s apprentice lineage was waking. The timesheet review kept Parker Meier’s work interval open, while reconciled timing notes left Oakley Brooks’s interval clear. At the instrument table, traces of Val Sato’s action showed a dormant chemical response; when the reviewers followed Winter Cohen’s intervention through the notes, that response came back clear. Location evidence placed Finley Meier’s workshop room at stable. The treatment order then separated two more records: sequence notes put Parker Meier at stable, and the sequence review kept Oakley Brooks at clear. For the protocol stream, token and seal checks left Val Sato’s tool stamp clear, while the sealed check showed Winter Cohen’s tool stamp open. With that, every evidence stream had a recorded status, though no single note had been allowed to settle the matter.
scenes.title: Timing the Treatment

scenes.prose: In the documentation office, the panel fed the reconstructed statuses through the prescribed passes, carrying each remainder forward through all 121 cycles. The incident’s accepted tally was 67. The final definition was deliberately strict: the certified restoration lead was the one person whose six-stream tally equaled that accepted tally. The reviewers closed the file without substituting a room, a reputation, or a persuasive memory for the formal comparison.
scenes.title: The Accepted Tally

title: Certified Restoration Lead — Case 10006
